stories.headline: Iran declares June peace deal void as US strikes reach Tehran and Semnan for the first time

key_facts.fact: The US intensified strikes early Thursday July 16, hitting targets further north than in previous rounds; Iranian state media reported strikes around Tehran and in Semnan province, home to Iran's ballistic missile production and space program.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. strikes early Thursday hit around Tehran, state media reported. It also reported that American attacks targeted Semnan province, home to Iran's ballistic missile production and space program.

key_facts.fact: US forces also fired into a ship the US accused of trying to break its naval blockade of Iran; Iran retaliated before dawn with missile and drone fire at US allies in the region and warned attacks may escalate.
key_facts.excerpt: American forces also fired into a ship the U.S. accused of trying to break its naval blockade on the Islamic Republic. Iran retaliated with missile and drone fire targeting U.S. allies in the region before dawn and warned its attacks may escalate.

key_facts.fact: Iranian officials say US strikes have killed more than 35 people and wounded over 300.
key_facts.excerpt: Already, Iranian officials say U.S. strikes have killed more than 35 people and wounded over 300 others.

key_facts.fact: Tehran said the repeated waves of US attacks voided the memorandum of understanding signed on June 17 that underpinned the ceasefire; top negotiator Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran was 'in an essential and existential war with America' and that its armed forces had 'complete freedom of action'.
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran said the repeated waves of US attacks had voided the memorandum of understanding with Washington that had underpinned the fragile ceasefire. Ghalibaf said Iran was 'in an essential and existential war with America' and had no reason to continue adhering to the terms of the peace agreement.

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC said it targeted the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain and a major US military logistics hub in Mina Abdullah, Kuwait; US strikes on Wednesday killed seven Iranian troops.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday morning, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain as part of a 'crushing response'. It said it also targeted a major US military logistics hub in Mina Abdullah, Kuwait.

key_facts.fact: The US military conducted rare daytime attacks on Wednesday including a 90-minute wave of strikes after reimposing a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran threatened to shut off more regional energy exports, saying the US 'must brace for the closure of all other export corridors that benefit the US and its allies'.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military on Wednesday launched rare daytime attacks on Iran, including a 90-minute wave of strikes, as it reimposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports. Tehran responded with strikes on 'US military targets' in Gulf states and threatened to halt energy exports in the region.

key_facts.fact: ISW reported US forces struck the Artesh Ground Forces 388th Mechanized Assault Brigade barracks in Iranshahr, roughly 200km inland from Iran's coast, killing seven soldiers and injuring 13, a notable expansion beyond July's coastal strike pattern.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian regime media reported on July 15 that US forces struck the Artesh Ground Forces 388th Mechanized Assault Brigade barracks in Iranshahr, Sistan and Baluchistan Province. The strikes reportedly killed seven Artesh soldiers, injured 13 others, and destroyed several buildings. This strike is notable given that the 388th Brigade is located around 200 kilometers from the Iranian coast.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude briefly topped $86 a barrel on July 15 before easing to $84.93, up 0.2%, after Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened to halt all Middle East energy exports; the Strait of Hormuz carried about a fifth of global oil and gas shipments before the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened July 15 to halt all energy exports from the Middle East because of the U.S. military's blockade to prevent tankers carrying Iranian oil from using the Strait of Hormuz. The price for a barrel of Brent crude briefly topped $86 in the morning before falling back to $84.93 per barrel, up 0.2% from the day before.

stories.headline: Uber agrees €13B takeover of Delivery Hero at €41.50 a share, with 14 markets sold to SSW Partners

key_facts.fact: Uber and Delivery Hero entered a business combination agreement on July 16, with Uber offering €41.50 per share in cash, implying a fully diluted equity value of €13.0 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Berlin, July 16, 2026 – Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) and one of its affiliates have entered into a business combination agreement with Delivery Hero SE (ETR: DHER)... Uber will offer Delivery Hero shareholders a cash consideration of €41.50 per share (the 'Offer Price'), implying a fully diluted equity value of €13.0 billion.

key_facts.fact: The offer price is a premium of about 127% on Delivery Hero's unaffected three-month volume-weighted average share price prior to May 8, 2026, and about 34% on the three-month VWAP prior to the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The Offer Price represents a premium of approximately 127% on the unaffected three-month volume-weighted average share price prior to May 8, 2026 and of approximately 34% on the three-month volume-weighted average share price prior to today's announcement.

key_facts.fact: The combination would extend Uber's platform to 99 countries with combined pro-forma GMV of $236 billion in 2025; Uber acquires 50 markets generating $42 billion of GMV in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: extending the world's largest mobility and delivery platform to a total of 99 countries, with combined pro-forma GMV of $236 billion in 2025... Businesses being acquired by Uber: 50 markets generating $42 billion of GMV in 2025

key_facts.fact: In parallel, New York investment firm SSW Partners agreed to buy Delivery Hero's businesses in 14 markets — where Uber Eats and Delivery Hero compete — generating €11 billion of GMV in 2025, for about €1.4 billion, conditioned on completion of the Uber offer.
key_facts.excerpt: SSW Partners will acquire Delivery Hero's businesses in a total of 14 markets, where Uber Eats and Delivery Hero compete, subject to completion of the Uber Takeover Offer and other customary conditions, for a consideration of approximately €1.4 billion.

key_facts.fact: Uber pledged to retain Delivery Hero's Berlin headquarters and make no changes to its Berlin workforce until at least 2029, and committed to use commercially reasonable efforts to invest €2 billion in Germany through 2031.
key_facts.excerpt: Uber... has pledged to retain Delivery Hero's headquarters and make no changes to its workforce in Berlin until at least 2029. Additionally, Uber committed to use commercially reasonable efforts to invest €2 billion in Germany through 2031.

key_facts.fact: The offer requires a minimum acceptance of 50% of shares plus one; Uber has irrevocable tender commitments for 16.68% which, with its 24.77% shareholding and 11.74% in instruments, would bring its total economic interest above 53%. Completion is expected in the second half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bidder has already received irrevocable tender commitments in relation to the Offer in the amount of 16.68%. Together with its shareholding of 24.77% and holding of instruments of 11.74%, Uber's total economic interest would amount to more than 53%. Completion of the Offer is expected to occur in the second half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The deal values Delivery Hero at about $14.8 billion; Uber's earlier offer in May was €33 per share.
key_facts.excerpt: Uber has agreed a €41.50-per-share takeover of Delivery Hero valuing it at $14.8bn. In May it offered €33. Fourteen markets go to SSW

stories.headline: EU and Ukraine sign drone production deal in Kyiv hours before Russian ballistic missiles kill two

key_facts.fact: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Kyiv and announced a new EU-Ukraine 'drone deal' at a ceremony marking Ukraine's Statehood Day, aiming to combine Kyiv's battlefield expertise with the EU's industrial capacity to scale up production.
key_facts.excerpt: The attack came hours after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Kyiv and announced a new 'drone deal' between Ukraine and the European Union. The agreement aims to combine Kyiv's battlefield expertise with the EU's industrial capacity to establish joint projects and rapidly scale up production.

key_facts.fact: Von der Leyen said the deal would 'bring together Ukrainian ingenuity and Europe's industrial scale', offering Kyiv 'huge technological and industrial capacity' alongside 'safe and secure production sites'.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking at a ceremony to mark Ukraine's Statehood Day, von der Leyen emphasised the need to 'combine our strengths', stating that the deal would 'bring together Ukrainian ingenuity and Europe's industrial scale'.

key_facts.fact: Russian ballistic missiles struck multiple districts of Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday July 16, killing two people and injuring six including a 16-year-old boy, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko.
key_facts.excerpt: Writing on Telegram in the early hours of Thursday, Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that two people were killed in the strikes, while six other residents were injured, including a 16-year-old boy.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's military said it struck six Russian tankers and two tugboats in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov overnight, saying the tankers carried Russian oil in circumvention of sanctions and fuel for Moscow's military.
key_facts.excerpt: Later on Thursday, Ukraine's military said it struck six Russian tankers and two tugboats in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov overnight. The tankers were being used to transport Russian oil and petroleum products in circumvention of international sanctions, as well as to transport fuel for Moscow's military, the general staff said on Telegram.

key_facts.fact: Outgoing UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer arrived in Kyiv on Thursday to meet Volodymyr Zelensky, a high-security trip before he is succeeded by Andy Burnham; Russia's defence ministry claimed it hit military and industrial facilities in Kyiv.
key_facts.excerpt: Keir Starmer, the outgoing Labour leader, arrived in Kyiv to meet Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday, a high-security trip before he leaves office. He is expected to assure Mr Zelensky that Britain's commitment to backing Ukraine will continue after he is succeeded by Andy Burnham... Russia's defence ministry claimed on Thursday it hit military and industrial facilities in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.

key_facts.fact: ISW reported that Russian forces resumed a strike campaign against Ukrainian Black Sea port infrastructure; agricultural consultant Bohdan Kostetskyi said on July 15 that recent Russian strikes on Ukrainian ports have effectively stopped deep-water grain exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Bohdan Kostetskyi, an operating partner at agricultural consulting agency Barva Invest, stated on July 15 that the recent Russian strikes against Ukrainian ports have effectively stopped deep-water grain exports.

stories.headline: AST SpaceMobile delays satellite-to-phone service to 2027 after Blue Origin blast, raises $1B

key_facts.fact: In a July 15 stock exchange filing, AST SpaceMobile said its launch campaign is targeting roughly 45 BlueBird satellites in early 2027, missing its late-2026 target for commercial service.
key_facts.excerpt: The Texas-based startup mentioned the delay in a stock exchange filing on Wednesday... in the Wednesday filing, the company writes that 'based on the Company's current expectations regarding launch availability, its launch campaign is targeting approximately 45 of its BlueBird satellites ("BB satellites") in early 2027.'

key_facts.fact: AST had been banking on Blue Origin to launch and operate 45 BlueBird satellites by the end of 2026, enabling it to serve partners AT&T and Verizon, before Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad in Florida.
key_facts.excerpt: AST was banking on Blue Origin to help it launch and operate 45 'BlueBird' satellites by the end of this year, enabling it to serve partners AT&T and Verizon... weeks after the company's launch provider Blue Origin suffered a major setback with its New Glenn rocket exploding.

key_facts.fact: On the same day, AST announced a $1 billion private offering of convertible senior notes due Feb. 1, 2034, with an option to add another $150 million.
key_facts.excerpt: AST SpaceMobile has put forward a $1 billion offering of convertible senior notes maturing in 2034, and could add another $150 million... The notes are due Feb. 1, 2034, and can convert into cash, Class A stock or a mix.

key_facts.fact: The notes carry a 1.625% annual interest rate and an initial conversion price of about $79.57 per share, a 20% premium to the July 15 closing price of $66.31; AST also entered capped call transactions with an initial cap price of $149.20.
key_facts.excerpt: The notes carry a 1.625% annual interest rate and an initial conversion price of about $79.57 per share, representing a 20% premium to the July 15 closing price of $66.31. The company also entered capped call transactions with an initial cap price of $149.20 per share, designed to reduce potential dilution if the notes are converted.

key_facts.fact: Preliminary cash was $2.723 billion at June 30, down from $3.459 billion at March 31 — a drop of about $736 million, or 21%.
key_facts.excerpt: Preliminary cash and... was $2.723 billion at June 30, down from $3.459 billion at March 31. That's a drop of around $736 million, or 21%.

key_facts.fact: AST said proceeds could fund partnerships and/or acquisitions to vertically integrate its business and 'mitigate risks associated with third-party launch providers'; shares fell to $58.03 after hours as investors weighed dilution.
key_facts.excerpt: The goal is to use the remaining proceeds to 'to pursue an expanding universe of growth initiatives and secure additional access to orbit for its space-based cellular broadband network, including partnerships and/or acquisitions to further vertically integrate its business and mitigate risks associated with third-party launch providers.'

stories.headline: SpaceX shares dip below their $135 IPO price for the first time as post-listing rally unravels

key_facts.fact: SpaceX shares fell for a fourth straight session on Wednesday July 15, briefly dropping below their $135 IPO price for the first time; the stock dipped about 1% and closed at $135.27.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX shares fell for a fourth-straight session on Wednesday, briefly dropping below their $135 initial public offering price for the first time as hype around the reusable rocket maker fizzled. The stock dipped about 1% on Wednesday and closed at $135.27 per share.

key_facts.fact: SPCX opened at $137.51, hit a low of $132.15 and a high of $139.34, closing at $135.27 on volume of 57.57 million shares.
The June 12 IPO raised nearly $86 billion — a record — and made Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire; the stock initially rose above $200 before losing value nearly every week since.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's shares fell to just above $135 on Wednesday, the price that CEO Elon Musk and his company chose ahead of its blockbuster June 12 IPO that raked in nearly $86 billion... SpaceX initially saw its stock price rise to more than $200 in the days after it went public, briefly giving it a valuation that rivaled tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft. Its shares have lost value basically every week since reaching that high point.

key_facts.fact: The reversal reflects investor concern over debt-funded AI spending and potential Fed rate hikes; SpaceX raised $25 billion in the bond market in June to build out technology infrastructure. Its first post-listing earnings report is expected in the first week of August.
key_facts.excerpt: The about-face in SpaceX reflects in part investor concern over debt-funded AI spending and what potential Federal Reserve rate hikes might do to stretched tech valuations. SpaceX turned to the bond market in June to raise US$25 billion... Investor focus will shift to the company's first results after listing. Analysts expect the report in the first week of August.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX joined the Nasdaq-100 last week under a rule change that shortened the eligibility period to 15 trading days for newly public companies, bringing passive index-tracking money into the stock.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week's induction into the Nasdaq-100 brought passive investors into the stock through index-tracking funds. The company was able to join the exchange due to a recent rule change that shortened the eligibility period to 15 trading days for newly public companies.

key_facts.fact: The stock has fallen more than 30% from highs of about $225; SpaceX is preparing the 13th test flight of Starship, with a 90-minute window opening at 6:45 p.m. ET Thursday, carrying next-generation Starlink V3 satellites for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares that debuted with enormous fanfare have now surrendered all of their gains from the opening print, falling more than 30% from highs of approximately $225... the company is preparing to conduct the thirteenth test flight of its Starship launch system with a 90-minute window opening at 6:45 p.m. ET on Thursday... while also introducing next-generation Starlink V3 satellites into space for the first time.

stories.headline: Fed officials signal no rate move as inflation runs near 4% and AI buildout heats the economy

key_facts.fact: The Federal Reserve released its July 2026 Beige Book on July 15, reporting that retail sales improved, the real estate sector was mixed, employment strengthened, wage pressures rose, and outlooks were stable to positive.
key_facts.excerpt: Retail sales improved, and the real estate sector was mixed. Employment strengthened, and wage pressures rose. Outlooks were stable to positive

key_facts.fact: In remarks in New York City on July 15, New York Fed President John Williams said overall inflation is 'unquestionably too high at about 4 percent,' well above the FOMC's 2 percent longer-run goal, and that 'the current stance of monetary policy is well positioned' to restore it.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Growth in the economy is solid and on trend, and the labor market is likewise solid and stable. But with inflation running high, it is imperative that we restore it to the Federal Reserve's 2 percent longer-run goal on a sustained basis. The current stance of monetary policy is well positioned to do that.'... overall inflation is 'unquestionably too high at about 4 percent'

key_facts.fact: Williams expects real GDP growth of around 2 to 2-1/4 percent this year and over the next two years, unemployment edging down to 4 percent in 2028, and inflation declining to around 3-1/4 percent by year-end before hitting the 2 percent target in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: He expects real GDP growth to be around 2 to 2-1/4 percent this year and over the next two years... he expects the unemployment rate to edge down very gradually to 4 percent in 2028. He expects overall inflation to decline to around 3-1/4 percent by year-end, then continue on a glide path toward the FOMC's 2 percent goal in 2027 before landing on target in 2028.

key_facts.fact: Fed Governor Lisa Cook said on July 15 that risks 'continue to be strongly weighted toward higher inflation,' that she voted to keep rates steady last month because tariffs and the Middle East conflict should produce only short-lived inflation increases, and that the 'data center buildout has added some heat to the economy.'
key_facts.excerpt: I voted with the rest of the FOMC last month to keep rates steady. I supported this stance, because the two main factors that have pushed up inflation over the past year—tariffs and the conflict in the Middle East—should, in theory, result in only short-lived increases in inflation... Going forward, though, I believe the risks continue to be strongly weighted toward higher inflation... data center buildout has added some heat to the economy.

key_facts.fact: Cook noted GDP growth in 2025 came in at 2.0 percent and FOMC participants now forecast 2.2 percent for 2026 — both about half a percentage point above last year's forecasts — with labor productivity growing about 2-1/2 percent per year over the past two years. The FOMC next meets in two weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: GDP growth in 2025 came in at 2.0 percent, and FOMC participants now forecast that 2026 will come in at 2.2 percent. Both readings exceed last year's forecasts by about 1/2 percentage point. Labor productivity is booming, having grown about 2-1/2 percent per year over the past two years... I look forward to engaging with my fellow Committee members at our next meeting in two weeks.

key_facts.fact: At its June 17 meeting the FOMC maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.
key_facts.excerpt: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's...

stories.headline: Brokerage infrastructure firm Alpaca raises $435M led by Peak XV to push into prime brokerage

key_facts.fact: Alpaca announced on July 16 a $135 million equity raise led by Peak XV with major participation from Elefund; total new financing reaches $435 million including debt financing primarily from Payward (Kraken's parent) and BMO.
key_facts.excerpt: Alpaca, a global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure, today announced a $135 million raise led by Peak XV, with major participation from Elefund... The new financing totals $435 million, inclusive of debt financing primarily from Payward, the parent company of global digital asset platform Kraken, and BMO.

key_facts.fact: The round follows Alpaca's $150 million Series D announced in January 2026, which valued the company at $1.15 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing builds on significant business growth as tokenization and AI reshape the industry, following Alpaca's $150 million Series D announced in January 2026, which valued the company at $1.15 billion

key_facts.fact: Alpaca said it has doubled revenue year over year for three consecutive years, surpassed $1.5 billion in assets under custody backing tokenized equities, and saw monthly active API users grow nearly 4x in the last six months.
key_facts.excerpt: Doubled revenue year over year for three consecutive years. Surpassed $1.5 billion in AUC for the underlying stocks backing tokenized equities. Monthly active API users grew nearly 4x during the last six months as Alpaca expanded agentic AI capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Alpaca will use the financing to accelerate its agent-first brokerage and API-first prime brokerage infrastructure; CEO Yoshi Yokokawa said Alpaca is 'uniquely positioned to become the default infrastructure layer for tokenized global capital markets and AI-native financial services.'
key_facts.excerpt: Alpaca will use the new financing to accelerate its agent-first brokerage and API-first prime brokerage infrastructure, enabling financial companies and institutional clients to build and scale investing products across traditional and onchain markets... 'Alpaca is uniquely positioned to become the default infrastructure layer for tokenized global capital markets and AI-native financial services,' said Yoshi Yokokawa, Co-Founder and CEO of Alpaca.

key_facts.fact: The company acquired an IFSCA-regulated broker-dealer in GIFT City India and UK/European regulated entities, completing passporting in all 30 EEA countries; it now supports over 10 million brokerage accounts across hundreds of fintechs and institutions in more than 40 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Acquired an IFSCA-regulated broker-dealer and payment service provider in GIFT City, establishing Alpaca's regulated presence in India. Acquired UK and European regulated entities and completed passporting in all 30 EEA countries... Today, Alpaca supports over 10 million brokerage accounts across hundreds of fintechs and institutions in more than 40 countries, backed by $400 million in funding.

key_facts.fact: Alpaca is exploring entry into prime broking with the $435 million raise.
key_facts.excerpt: Alpaca, which offers brokerage and financial infrastructure, raised $135M in equity and $300M in debt, following a $150M Series D in January
